The '''2014–15 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|111th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|84th consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. It covered a period from 1 July 2014 to 30 June 2015. This was also legendary goalkeeper [[Iker Casillas]]'s 16th and last season at Real Madrid and in La Liga.

After a slow start to the season, Real Madrid went on a record-breaking 22-match winning streak, which included wins against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], surpassing the previous Spanish record of 18 successive wins set by [[Frank Rijkaard]]'s Barça in the [[2005–06 FC Barcelona season|2005–06 season]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30406666 "Real Madrid stretch winning run as Ronaldo and Gareth Bale score"]. BBC. Retrieved 20 December 2014</ref> In late December, Real Madrid won their first [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup|Club World Cup]], defeating [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] 2–0 in the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/2-0-world-champions|title=2–0: World champions!|date=20 December 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> The winning streak came to an end in their opening match of 2015 with a loss to Valencia, leaving the club two short of equalling the world record of 24 consecutive wins.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30673410 "Valencia 2 – 1 Real Madrid"]. BBC. Retrieved 4 January 2015</ref> Madrid was in contention for both the [[2014–15 La Liga|La Liga]] title and the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] until the very end but ultimately came up short, finishing with 92 points in the league, two behind [[Treble (association football)|treble-winning]] Barcelona and losing their Champions League crown to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] 2–3 on aggregate in the Champions League semi-finals. [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] finished the season scoring 48 league goals, winning his fourth [[European Golden Shoe]], and 61 goals in all competitions, breaking his record from [[2011–12 Real Madrid CF season|2011–12]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2465540-comparing-cristiano-ronaldos-201415-stats-to-his-201314-numbers|title = Comparing Cristiano Ronaldo's 2014/15 Stats to His 2013/14 Numbers|website = [[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> 

Overall, despite playing an attractive attacking football and being the highest scoring team in Europe with 118 league goals,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/06/james-and-bale-la-ligas-top-scoring-midfielders|title=James and Bale, La Liga's top scoring midfielders|quote=Fourteen Madrid players have chipped in to score a record 118 goals with which the team closed out the La Liga campaign.|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=8 June 2015}}</ref> several heartbreaking defeats meant that Real finished the season with two trophies out of six possible, which contributed to the dismissal of [[Carlo Ancelotti]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/05/florentino-perez-holds-a-press-conference|title=Florentino Pérez holds a press conference|date=25 May 2015|website=Realmadrid.com}}</ref> Ancelotti would return to coach the team in [[2021–22 Real Madrid CF season|2021]].

==Season overview==
===Pre-season===
On 25 June 2014, [[Zinedine Zidane]] was named as the coach of [[Real Madrid Castilla]] and would manage the B team,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/06/zidane-to-manage-castilla-in-the-2014/2015-season|title=Zidane to manage Castilla in the 2014/2015 season|date=25 June 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> while Real Madrid confirmed the appointment of [[Fernando Hierro]] as an assistant coach to [[Carlo Ancelotti]], replacing Zidane.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/07/10/en/football/real_madrid/1405017376.html|title=Fernando Hierro, Ancelotti's new right-hand-man|date=10 July 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref>

Real Madrid's pre-season began on 14 July. Ancelotti had 22 players at his disposal, including 12 from Castilla. The players who were involved in the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] were still on vacation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/07/real-madrids-2014/15-season-is-underway|title=Real Madrid's 2014/15 season is underway|date=14 July 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

On 17 July, Madrid signed World Cup winner [[Toni Kroos]] on a six-year deal for a fee around €25&nbsp;million to €30&nbsp;million. Kroos became Madrid's first summer signing of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/Official-Statement-Toni-Kroos|title=Official statement|date=17 July 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thelocal.de/20140717/german-toni-kroos-signs-for-real-madrid-from-bayern-munich|title=Toni Kroos leaves Bayern Munich for Real Madrid|work=The Local|date=17 July 2014|access-date=17 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/toni-kroos/wechsel-zu-real-madrid-perfekt-36846438.bild.html|title=WM-Held Kroos wechselt zu Real|work=Bild|date=17 July 2014|access-date=17 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/116842/real-madrid-to-pay-e30m-for-toni-kroos-be-presented-at-5pm-on-thursday/ |title=Real Madrid to pay €30m for Toni Kroos, be presented at 5pm on Thursday |work=Inside Spanish Football |date=17 July 2014 |access-date=17 July 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720050513/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/116842/real-madrid-to-pay-e30m-for-toni-kroos-be-presented-at-5pm-on-thursday/ |archive-date=20 July 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jul/17/toni-kroos-joins-real-madrid|title=Guardian:toni-kroos-joins-real-madrid|date=17 July 2014|access-date=17 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Jiménez|first1=Rubén|title=Willkommen Kroos!|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/07/17/en/football/real_madrid/1405581624.html|access-date=17 July 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=17 July 2014}}</ref>

[[Álvaro Morata]] was sold to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] for a fee of €20&nbsp;million, while Madrid retained the option of resigning him for a fee of €30&nbsp;million after the first year and €36&nbsp;million after the second,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/07/official-announcement-morata|title=Official announcement: Morata|date=19 July 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>[http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/06baf795-883a-4ca9-80e9-beba5def3cfd/comunicato+19072014+morata+eng.pdf?MOD=AJPERES Press release: Juventus]{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> while [[Denis Cheryshev]] and [[Casemiro]] were loaned to [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] and [[FC Porto|Porto]] respectively for the upcoming season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/06/official-announcement-2|title=Official announcement|date=28 June 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/07/official-statement-casemiro|title=Official announcement: Casemiro|date=19 July 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

On 21 July, Madrid set off on their pre-season tour of the United States. Nineteen players were among the travelling party, with Ancelotti opting to take nine from Real Madrid Castilla to compensate for the absences of Madrid's World Cup players, who remained on holiday. However, [[Xabi Alonso]], [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] and [[Fábio Coentrão]] did fly to the U.S. and cut their summer breaks short and joined the rest of the team. [[Jesé]] stayed in Madrid to go on with his treatment at Valdebebas.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/07/ancelotti-will-take-20-players-to-the-us|title=Ancelotti will take 20 players to the US|date=21 July 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/07/real-madrid-usa-tour-2014-summer|title=Real Madrid USA Tour (2014 Summer)|date=21 July 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

Madrid reached an agreement with [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] on 22 July for [[2014 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] Golden Boot winner [[James Rodríguez]], who signed a six-year contract for a fee of €75&nbsp;million, becoming the [[Transfer (association football)|fourth most expensive player]] in world football, behind [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], [[Gareth Bale]] and [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/07/official-announcement-james-rodriguez|title=Official announcement: James Rodríguez|date=22 July 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28418131|title=James Rodriguez: Real Madrid sign Monaco forward|date=22 July 2014|work=bbc.co}}</ref>

===August===
On 3 August, Costa Rican goalkeeper [[Keylor Navas]] was signed from [[Levante UD|Levante]] for €10&nbsp;million following his exuberant performances at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-statement-keylor-navas|title=Official statement: Keylor Navas|date=3 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

A day later, [[Jesús Fernández Collado|Jesús Fernández]] switched sides and joined Levante for a reported fee of €500,000.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-statement-jesus-fernandez|title=Official statement: Jesús Fernández|date=4 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

In their first competitive match of the season, Madrid played [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup|2014 edition]] of the [[UEFA Super Cup]]. The game saw the debuts of World Cup stars [[James Rodríguez]] and [[Toni Kroos]], as Madrid defeated the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League|winners]]. On the half-hour mark, [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] broke the deadlock and helped Madrid to a lead 1–0 at half time. In the second half, it was again Ronaldo who scored and the game ended 2–0, with Madrid capturing their second Super Cup title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/2-0-european-super-cup-champions|title=2–0: European Super Cup Champions!|date=12 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28741099|title=Super Cup: Cristiano Ronaldo scores twice in Real Madrid win|date=12 August 2014|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

The following day, Madrid had reached an agreement with [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] for the transfer of [[Diego López Rodríguez|Diego López]] to the Italian club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-statement-diego-lopez|title=Official statement: Diego López|date=13 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

In the [[2014 Supercopa de España]] against [[Atlético Madrid]], the first leg ended with a 1–1 draw after goals from [[James Rodríguez]] and [[Raúl García (footballer, born 1986)|Raúl García]], going into the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium|Estadio Vicente Calderón]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/1-1-the-supercup-of-spain-will-be-decided-in-the-calderon|title=1–1: The Supercup of Spain will be decided in the Calderón|date=19 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> [[Mario Mandžukić]] shocked Real early on after just two minutes in the second leg with the only goal of the match, which meant that Atlético won the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/1-0-a-lack-of-accuracy-did-for-real-madrid-in-the-supercopa-de-espana|title=1–0: A lack of accuracy did for Real Madrid in the Supercopa de España|date=22 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014/supercopa_espana/final/vuelta/atm_rma/|title=Una pequeña revancha|date=23 August 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref>

After months of speculation, [[Ángel Di María]] completed his move to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] for a British record fee of €75&nbsp;million (£59.7M) on 26 August. The deal also included a possible of €5.5&nbsp;million (£4.3M) in add-ons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2014/Aug/manchester-united-sign-angel-di-maria-from-real-madrid.aspx |title=United sign Angel Di Maria for record fee |date=26 August 2014|work=Manchester United.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-announcement-di-maria|title=Official Announcement: Di María|date=26 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/08/27/en/football/real_madrid/1409135850.html|title=Di María balances Bernabéu books |date=27 August 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref>

[[Xabi Alonso]] joined [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] for €10&nbsp;million on 29 August 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-announcement-xabi-alonso|title=Official announcement: Xabi Alonso|date=29 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbayern.de/de/news/news/2014/wechsel-von-xabi-alonso-perfekt.php|title=Xabi Alonso ist jetzt ein Bayer|date=29 August 2014|work=fcbayern.de}}</ref>

After winning their first [[2014–15 La Liga|league]] match against [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]] 2–0 by goals from [[Karim Benzema]] and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/2-0-benzema-and-cristiano-ronaldo-provide-the-first-la-liga-victory|title=2–0: Benzema and Cristiano Ronaldo provide the first La Liga victory|date=25 August 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> Madrid lost their first game in this year's league campaign at [[Real Sociedad]] 2–4. Even though ''Los Blancos'' took the early two-goal lead by [[Sergio Ramos]] and [[Gareth Bale]], Sociedad tied the game at halftime before they went on to score two more in the second half.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/09/01/futbol/equipos/real_sociedad/1409581512.html|title=Zubikarai, contento tras su actuación ante el Madrid|date=31 August 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28996955|title=Real Sociedad 4–2 Real Madrid|date=31 August 2014|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

===September===
On 1 September 2014, Madrid signed [[Javier Hernández]] on a season-long loan deal from [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. Real Madrid had an option to buy the player for a fee of €22&nbsp;million next season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/09/official-announcement-javier-hernandez-chicharito|title=Official announcement: Javier Hernández 'Chicharito'|date=1 September 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2014/Sep/javier-chicharito-hernandez-joins-real-madrid-on-season-long-loan.aspx|title=Chicharito joins Real Madrid on loan|date=1 September 2014|publisher=Manchester United F.C.}}</ref> He became Real Madrid's first Mexican player in 22 years, with [[Hugo Sánchez]] having been the last one to play for the club up to that point.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/09/01/en/football/real_madrid/1409602937.html|title=Chicharito – 1st Real Mexican since Hugo Sánchez|date=1 September 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref>

The league match between Real and Atlético was their third meeting of this season already in September.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/09/1-2-real-madrid-deserved-more-in-the-derby|title=1–2: Real Madrid deserved more in the derby|date=13 September 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> After the visitors took an early lead, Ronaldo equalized through a penalty before [[Arda Turan]] scored the decisive goal 14 minutes before the end of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29176277|title=Real Madrid 1–2 Atl Madrid|date=13 September 2014|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

In their first [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match after winning ''La Decima'', Madrid got off to a good start by defeating Basel 5–1, scoring four goals in 22 minutes during the first half.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/09/5-1-a-goal-fest-and-top-of-the-group-start-for-the-reigning-champions-league-holders|title=5–1: A goal fest and top-of-the-group start for the reigning Champions League holders|date=16 September 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

Real Madrid then faced [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] at the [[Estadio Riazor|Riazor]], then the only stadium in the league at which Ronaldo had not scored in. Real went on to produce a thumping 8–2 win, with a hat-trick from Ronaldo, braces by Bale and Hernández, and James chipping in with a goal. This also marked the first time that Real had scored eight goals on the road in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29275785|title=Deportivo de La Coruña 2–8 Real Madrid|date=20 September 2014|publisher=BBC}}</ref> With that, Real scored 13 goals in just two matches in a span of four days. Madrid continued their fine scoring form with a 5–1 win over [[Elche CF]], with Ronaldo scoring four times.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/primera/jornada_5/rma_elc/|title=Cristiano hace y deshace|date=23 September 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref>

A goal each from [[Luka Modrić]] and Ronaldo helped Real beat [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] 2–0, with Ronaldo scoring his tenth league goal in only five games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/primera/jornada_6/vil_rma/|title=Cuestión de clase|date=27 September 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref>

===October===
In the Champions League, Madrid took on newcomers [[PFC Ludogorets Razgrad|Ludogorets Razgrad]]. After a surprising start, a missed penalty and being down 0–1, Ronaldo and Benzema were able to turn the game around to a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/10/1-2-victory-in-sofia-and-sole-leaders|title=1–2: Victory in Sofia and sole leaders|date=1 October 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

Back to the league campaign, Madrid took on [[Athletic Bilbao]] at home and came up with a convincing 5–0 victory, thanks to a hat-trick from Ronaldo and a brace from Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/primera/jornada_7/rma_ath/|title=Real Madrid y nada más|date=5 October 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref>

After the international break, Madrid faced [[Levante UD|Levante]] on the road. Ronaldo got the scoring going with a penalty and Hernández pushed the lead to 2–0 at half-time. After the break, Ronaldo added his second, with James and [[Isco]] chipped in the other goals to make it a 5–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29657726|title=Levante 0–5 Real Madrid|date=18 October 2014|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

In the third matchday of the Champions League, Madrid visited [[Anfield]] to face [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]. Ronaldo scored a spectacular flick and Benzema added a brace to give ''Los Blancos'' a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/10/0-3-historic-thumping-win-at-anfield|title=0–3: Historic thumping win at Anfield|date=22 October 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

Back to La Liga, Real took on [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in another edition of ''[[El Clásico]]''. Despite an early shock by [[Neymar]], Ronaldo was able to tie the game by half-time. [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] and Benzema then scored in the second half to give Madrid a 3–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/la-pegada-del-real-madrid-decide-el-clasico|title=La pegada del Real Madrid decide el clásico|date=25 October 2014|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

Starting the [[2014–15 Copa del Rey]] campaign, Madrid took on [[UE Cornellà|Cornellà]] while resting several first team squad members. Two goals from [[Raphaël Varane]] and one each from Hernández and [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] gave Real a 4–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/real-madrid-y-sevilla-vencen-en-sus-compromisos-coperos|title=Real Madrid y Sevilla vencen en sus compromisos coperos|date=29 October 2014|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

===November===
The new month started with an away trip to [[Granada CF|Granada]], which was ended successfully in a 4–0 victory after goals from Ronaldo, a Rodríguez brace and Benzema. This marked the seventh straight win for Real.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-alcanza-su-septimo-triunfo-consecutivo|title=El Real Madrid alcanza su séptimo triunfo consecutivo|date=1 November 2014|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

Taking on Liverpool at the fourth matchday of the Champions League campaign, Real was able to get a narrow 1–0 victory, by a goal from Benzema. With this victory, Real booked their spot in the round of 16 two matchdays before the group stage concluded.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/11/1-0-through-to-the-champions-league-round-of-16|title=1–0: Through to the Champions League Round of 16|date=4 November 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

Before the international break, Madrid took on [[Rayo Vallecano]]. Bale, who returned from injury, and Ramos got ''Los Blancos'' a 2–0 lead, which was reduced to a one-goal lead at half-time. [[Toni Kroos]] with his first goal for Madrid, Benzema and Ronaldo then produced a convincing second half display and lifted Real to a 5–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-continua-intratable-en-la-liga-bbva|title=El Real Madrid continúa intratable en la Liga BBVA|date=8 November 2014|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

With Modrić sidelined due to an injury sustained while on national team duty (that eventually kept him out until early March),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/11/modric-medical-report|title=Modric medical report|date=17 November 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> Madrid took on [[SD Eibar]] for the first time in club history. Real got a 4–0 victory after a brace from Ronaldo and goals from James and Benzema, which secured their top position in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/30126423|title=Eibar 0–4 Real Madrid|date=17 November 2014|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

Thanks to a goal from Ronaldo, Madrid won against Basel in the Champions League, which marked their 15th consecutive win in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/11/0-1-ronaldo-seals-the-top-spot-for-madrids-passage-into-the-round-of-16|title=0–1: Ronaldo seals the top spot for Madrid's passage into the Round of 16|date=26 November 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

In an away match at [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], Real was able to squeeze out a 1–2 win after goals from Benzema and Bale. This marked team's 16th win in a row and their second "perfect" month of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/un-real-madrid-de-record-vence-al-malaga|title=Un Real Madrid de récord vence al Málaga|date=29 November 2014|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

===December===
In their second leg match against Cornellà, Ancelotti again opted to rest regular starters and give other players a chance. The game also marked the return of [[Jesé]], who also scored in a 5–0 victory (9–1 on aggregate), alongside a brace from Rodríguez, a goal from Isco and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-primer-clasificado-para-octavos-de-la-copa-del-rey|title=El Real Madrid, primer clasificado para octavos de la Copa del Rey|date=3 December 2014|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

Playing with their regular starter team, Madrid took on [[Celta de Vigo]] and won 3–0, thanks to a hat-trick by Ronaldo, who reached the milestone of 200 league goals for Real Madrid. It was Ronaldo's fourth hat-trick of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/cristiano-ronaldo-continues-setting-records-as-real-madrid-flourish-120614|title=Cristiano Ronaldo continues setting records as Real Madrid flourish|date=6 December 2014|work=Fox Sports}}</ref>

Madrid finished up the group stage of the Champions League with a 4–0 victory over Ludogorets Razgrad with goals from Ronaldo, Bale, [[Álvaro Arbeloa]] and [[Álvaro Medrán]]. Real repeated its feat from the [[2011–12 Real Madrid CF season|2011–12 season]], winning all six Champions League group stage games, an achievement not matched by any other team in the tournament's history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/4-0-a-goal-fest-to-close-out-a-perfect-group-stage|title=4–0: A goal fest to close out a perfect Group Stage|date=9 December 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> With that win, Madrid set a new record in Spanish football by winning their 19th-straight game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/real-madrid/story/2189750/real-madrid-win-19th-straight-in-all-competitions-to-set-spanish-record|title=Real Madrid win 19th straight in all competitions to set Spanish record|date=9 December 2014|work=espnfc.com}}</ref>

Real Madrid extended their streak to 20 consecutive wins with a 4–1 victory against [[UD Almería|Almería]] after a brace from Ronaldo and goals from Isco and Bale.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-no-falla-en-almeria|title=El Real Madrid no falla en Almería|date=12 December 2014|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

Their next game took place at the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup]] against [[Cruz Azul]] in the semi-finals. Goals from Ramos, Bale, Benzema and Isco secured a 4–0 victory and a place in the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/0-4-real-madrid-reach-the-final-of-the-club-world-cup|title=0–4: Real Madrid reach the final of the Club World Cup!|date=16 December 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref>

The final was won 2–0 against [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] of Argentina after goals by Ramos and Bale. It was the first Club World Cup title for Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/2-0-world-champions|title=2–0: World champions!|date=20 December 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.}}</ref> It was also their 22nd consecutive win in the current season.

===January===
The new year started off with an away game at the [[Mestalla Stadium]] facing [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]. Even though Ronaldo got Real in front, Madrid was not able to close the game and lost 1–2. This was the team's first loss after 22 straight wins.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/match/402467/valencia-real-madrid/report|title=Real Madrid's run comes to an end as Valencia triumph in La Liga|date=4 January 2015|work=espnfc.com}}</ref>

Facing Atlético Madrid in the first leg of the Copa del Rey round of 16, ''Los Blancos'' were not able to come away with a win, losing [[Madrid derby|El Derbi madrileño]] 0–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/30688019|title=Atlético Madrid 2–0 Real Madrid|date=7 January 2015 | publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], goals from Rodríguez, Bale and [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]], who scored his first professional goal for Madrid, secured Real a 3–0 victory to get back on track after two consecutive losses.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-se-reencuentra-con-la-victoria|title=El Real Madrid se reencuentra con la victoria|date=10 January 2015|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

In the second leg of the Copa del Rey round of 16, Real needed to cancel out Atlético's two-goal advantage. Ronaldo and Ramos scored, but that was not enough, as Madrid conceded two, and the match ended 2–2 and 2–4 on aggregate, therefore ending Real's attempt to defend the Copa del Rey title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/torres-double-dumps-real-madrid-cup-211936430--sow.html|title=Torres double dumps Real Madrid out of Cup|publisher=Yahoo! Sport|access-date=16 January 2015}}</ref>

Against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], Madrid was able to squeeze a 3–0 victory after a second half Ronaldo brace and a goal from Bale.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/cristiano-y-bale-deciden-en-getafe|title=Cristiano y Bale deciden en Getafe|date=18 January 2015|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

In the transfer period, Madrid signed [[Martin Ødegaard]] and [[Lucas Silva (footballer, born 1993)|Lucas Silva]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2015/01/23/8210972/real-madrid-sign-lucas-silva|title=The midfielder has ended speculation by putting pen to paper on a lengthy contract with the European champions|date=23 January 2015|work=goal.com}}</ref> Ødegaard would only train with the first team but play with [[Real Madrid Castilla]].<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30927958 | title=Odegaard completes Real Madrid move | work=BBC Sport }}</ref>

Starting the second half of the season at Córdoba, Real needed a late penalty converted by Bale to come away with a 2–1 victory. Benzema scored the equalizer in the first half while Ronaldo was sent off by the referee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-remonta-ante-un-cordoba-convincente|title=El Real Madrid remonta ante un Córdoba convincente|date=24 January 2015|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

A brace from Benzema and goals from Rodríguez and Ramos secured a 4–1 home victory for Madrid against Real Sociedad to finish January.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/remontada-y-victoria-del-real-madrid|title=Remontada y victoria del Real Madrid|date=31 January 2015|work=lfp.es}}</ref>

===February===
In their first match of February, Real earned a 2–1 win against Sevilla, with goals from Rodríguez and Jesé.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/328831/report|title=Primera Division: Real Madrid beat Sevilla 2–1 to move four points clear|work=skysports.com|date=5 February 2015}}</ref>

Without five regular starters, Real suffered a 0–4 loss against Atlético, with goals from [[Tiago Mendes|Tiago]], [[Saúl Ñíguez|Saúl]] (who scored a beautiful overhead kick), [[Antoine Griezmann]] and [[Mario Mandžukić]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-atletico-se-impone-en-el-derbi-madrileno|title=El Atlético se impone en el derbi madrileño|work=lfp.es|date=7 February 2015}}</ref>

Goals from Isco and Benzema gave Madrid a 2–0 victory against Deportivo.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-responde-ante-un-aguerrido-deportivo|title=El Real Madrid responde ante un aguerrido Deportivo|work=lfp.es|date=14 February 2015}}</ref>

In a rematch of last year's round of 16 in the Champions League against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]], Real secured a 2–0 first leg away victory with goals from Ronaldo and Marcelo.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/02/0-2-real-madrid-pave-their-way-to-the-quarter-finals|title=0–2: Real Madrid pave their way to the quarter-finals|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=18 February 2015}}</ref>

Goals from Benzema and Ronaldo against Elche gave Real a four-point gap at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-se-consolida-en-el-martinez-valero|title=El Real Madrid se consolida en el Martínez Valero|work=lfp.es|date=22 February 2015}}</ref>

===March===
[[File:Ronaldo vs. FC Schalke 04 (16854146922).jpg|thumb|left|150px|[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] in action against Schalke 04]]
A goal from Ronaldo, which made him the first player to score over 30 goals in five consecutive seasons in a European top league,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsjoe.ie/football/vine-cristiano-ronaldo-becomes-first-player-to-score-30-goals-in-five-consecutive-seasons-in-any-of-europes-major-leagues/15675|title=Cristiano Ronaldo becomes first player to score 30+ goals in five consecutive seasons in any of Europe's major leagues|work=sportsjoe.ie|date=1 March 2015}}</ref> was not enough to get past Villarreal, as the game ended 1–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/emocion-futbol-e-igualdad-en-el-bernabeu|title=Emoción, fútbol e igualdad en el Bernabéu|work=lfp.es|date=1 March 2015}}</ref>

Madrid visited Bilbao the next matchday and lost 0–1, with a header from [[Aritz Aduriz]] in the 26th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-athletic-continua-euforico|title=El Athletic continúa eufórico|work=lfp.es|date=7 March 2015}}</ref>

Taking on Schalke in the return leg of the round of 16 in the Champions League, Real had their hands full not to get knocked out. Two goals from Ronaldo and another one from Benzema saved Real's victory on aggregate, even though they lost the game 3–4.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/03/3-4-real-madrid-qualify-for-the-champions-league-quarter-finals|title=3–4: Real Madrid qualify for the Champions League quarter-finals|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=11 March 2015}}</ref>

A first-half brace from Bale gave Madrid a 2–0 win against Levante before the ''Clásico''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31880430|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Levante|publisher=BBC|date=15 March 2015}}</ref>

Real suffered a major setback in the title race after losing to Barcelona 1–2 away from home. Ronaldo scored the lone goal for Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-fc-barcelona-se-lleva-el-clasico|title=El FC Barcelona se lleva el clásico|work=lfp.es|date=22 March 2015}}</ref>

===April===
On 1 April, Madrid confirmed the signing of [[FC Porto|Porto]] and [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] full back [[Danilo (footballer, born July 1991)|Danilo]] for a fee of €31&nbsp;million on a five-year deal; he would join the squad at the beginning of the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/03/official-announcement-danilo|title=Official Announcement: Danilo|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=1 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32141669|title=Real Madrid to sign £23m defender from Porto|publisher=BBC|date=1 April 2015}}</ref>

Coming out of the international break, Real thrashed Granada 9–1 at the Bernabéu, with Ronaldo scoring five goals. The other goals came from Bale, a brace from Benzema and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/cristiano-brilla-con-un-repoker-de-goles|title=Cristiano brilla con un repóker de goles|work=lfp.es|date=5 April 2015}}</ref>

Playing at Vallecano, Madrid was held scoreless until minutes after the hour mark before Ronaldo and Rodríguez helped Real to get a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/ronaldo-y-james-desactivan-a-un-solido-rayo|title=Ronaldo y James desactivan a un sólido Rayo|work=lfp.es|date=8 April 2015}}</ref>

Goals from Ronaldo, Hernández and Jesé gave Madrid a 3–0 win over Eibar while resting some key players.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-supera-otra-prueba-ante-el-eibar|title=El Real Madrid supera otra prueba ante el Eibar|work=lfp.es|date=11 April 2015}}</ref>

Real visited the Vicente Calderón to play their local rivals Atlético Madrid in the first leg of the quarter-finals in the Champions League. The match ended in a goalless draw. This was the seventh time both teams faced each other this season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/04/0-0-the-tie-will-be-decided-at-the-bernabeu|title=0–0: The tie will be decided at the Bernabéu|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=14 April 2015}}</ref>

Against Málaga, ''Los Blancos'' were able to get a 3–1 victory after goals from Ramos, Rodríguez and Ronaldo.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-sigue-en-la-pelea-por-la-liga-bbva|title=El Real Madrid sigue en la pelea por la Liga BBVA|work=lfp.es|date=18 April 2015}}</ref> The goal by Ronaldo meant he had scored at least 50 goals for the fifth consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2015/04/18/10905932/cristiano-ronaldo-scores-50-goals-five-seasons-in-a-row|title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores 50 goals five seasons in a row|work=goal.com|date=18 April 2015}}</ref>

A late goal from Hernández after a brilliant solo run by Ronaldo gave Real their first victory in eight matches against Atlético this season and helped them reach the semi-finals of the Champions League for the fifth consecutive time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/04/1-0-through-to-the-semi-finals-of-the-champions-league|title=1–0: Through to the semi-finals of the Champions League!|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=22 April 2015}}</ref>

A brace from Hernández and goals from Rodríguez and Kroos gave Madrid a 2–4 win at Vigo to keep their title dreams alive.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-logra-el-triunfo-y-sigue-en-la-lucha-por-el-titulo|title=El Real Madrid logra el triunfo y sigue en la lucha por el título|work=lfp.es|date=26 April 2015}}</ref>

In a midweek game, Real was able to get past Almería by a score of 3–0, thanks to a goal from Álvaro Arbeloa, an own goal and a wonder goal from Rodríguez.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-no-cede-ante-el-almeria|title=El Real Madrid no cede ante el Almería|work=lfp.es|date=29 April 2015}}</ref>

===May===
A hat-trick from Ronaldo propelled Madrid to a 3–2 win over Sevilla. This was Sevilla's first home defeat since 13 March 2014, when they lost 2–0 to [[Real Betis|Betis]] in the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] round of 16, and their first home league defeat since 9 February 2014, when they lost 4–1 to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/cristiano-ronaldo-derriba-la-fortaleza-del-sevilla|title=Cristiano Ronaldo derriba la fortaleza del Sevilla|work=lfp.es|date=2 May 2015}}</ref>

Despite a goal from Ronaldo, Real came up short in the first leg of the Champions League semi-finals against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], losing 1–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/04/1-0-through-to-the-semi-finals-of-the-champions-league|title=2–1: Comeback required in the Bernabéu in order to reach the final|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=5 May 2015}}</ref>

A 2–2 draw against Valencia, with goals from Pepe and Isco, damaged the hopes of winning the league title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-se-aleja-del-titulo|title=El Real Madrid se aleja del título|work=lfp.es|date=9 May 2015}}</ref>

The return leg against Juventus ended in a 1–1 draw, and the dream of defending the Champions League title was shattered in the semi-finals. Ronaldo scored again and finished the competition with 10 goals, tied for most.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/05/1-1-the-holders-gave-it-their-all-right-to-the-end|title=1–1: The holders gave it their all right to the end|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=13 May 2015}}</ref>

Ronaldo scored a brilliant hat-trick, but a 4–1 victory over Espanyol was not enough to capture the title as Barcelona won their game against Atlético Madrid 1–0, which assured Real Madrid the second place until the end of the season. This was Ronaldo's seventh hat-trick of the season.

In their last match of the season, Real hosted Getafe and defeated them 7–3 with yet another hat-trick from Ronaldo, who finished the season scoring 61 goals in all competitions, breaking his own record from [[2011–12 Real Madrid CF season|2011–12]]. The Portuguese also became the highest scoring ''Madridista'' for the sixth consecutive season. He would go on to accomplish the feat every season until [[2017–18 Real Madrid CF season|2018]] when he left the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2465540-comparing-cristiano-ronaldos-201415-stats-to-his-201314-numbers|title = Comparing Cristiano Ronaldo's 2014/15 Stats to His 2013/14 Numbers|website = [[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/fiesta-de-goles-para-cerrar-la-liga-bbva-2014-15|title=Fiesta de goles para cerrar la Liga BBVA 2014–15|work=lfp.es|date=23 May 2015}}</ref>
